# technitium_app_config (Resource)

Manages the config of an installed DNS app. The format is the app's own, usually JSON. Destroying the resource leaves the config as it is. Uninstalling or replacing the app deletes its config: add `replace_triggered_by` on the `technitium_app` to set it again in the same apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_app" "config_split_horizon" {
  name = "Split Horizon"
  url  = "https://download.technitium.com/dns/apps/SplitHorizonApp-v11.zip"
}

resource "technitium_app_config" "split_horizon" {
  name = technitium_app.config_split_horizon.name
  config = jsonencode({
    networks = {
      lan = ["192.168.0.0/16"]
    }
  })

  # Uninstalling or replacing the app makes the server delete its config.
  # This sets it again in the same apply.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [technitium_app.config_split_horizon]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `config` (String, Sensitive) The app's config as JSON, for example from `jsonencode(...)`. Differences in spacing and key order alone are not changes.
- `name` (String) The name of the installed app.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import technitium_app_config.split_horizon "Split Horizon"
```
